decisions.note: p.064 ends with a short last line ([آل عمران: ١٦٠].) and the first line of p.065 «(وَأَيِّدْنِي…» is indented like «(الله. الله. الله)» lower on the page, so this is a new paragraph and there is no '+'.

The words are visibly bold. The parentheses look the same as regular ones: measured at 2000 dpi, the bold-span parens and the regular parens of «(ثلاثًا)» on p.068 have the same stroke (31 px) and ink. They do not contrast, so they stay outside the ** markers.
Same as d002: the bold words are inside the markers and the parentheses, which look like regular ones, are outside.
[الفجر:٢٧-٢٨] is set tight: the gap after the colon is only the glyph side-bearing, while [المجادلة: ٢٢] on the same page shows a clear space. The parentheses stay outside the bold, as in d002.
Closing parenthesis has the same weight as a regular one, so it goes outside the bold (see d002).
«(الله. الله. الله)»: the words are bold and the parentheses look regular, so they go outside the markers (see d002).
At 1200 dpi the nun of يَكُن has no sukun. The sukun is on لَمْ only.
At 1200 dpi قَوِيٌ has a kasra under the waw and dammatan on the yeh, with no shadda (a print error kept as printed).

In the lam-mim ligature, the lam's sukun is drawn as a small filled mark stacked on the mim's damma, the same mark as in المُحَجَّلِينَ and المُذْنِبِينَ. There is no mark at all over the ra (checked at 2000 dpi). So it is الْمُرسَلِينَ.
The lam's sukun is stacked above the mim's damma in the ligature (the same filled mark as in d009/d011), so it is الْمُتَّقِينَ.
At 3000 dpi the stacked lam sukun is visible above the damma in both words. In المذنبين the dhal also has its own hook sukun.
At 1500 dpi the hook-shaped sukun over the lam is clearly printed above the kha's fatha in الْخَيْرِ and above the ha's damma in الْهُدَىٰ.
At 2500 dpi the ain of نعتك has a fatha stroke, not the hook sukun used in وَصْفِكَ just before it. So it is وَنَعَتِكَ (print error kept).
At 1500 dpi the hook sukun over the lam of بِالْمَعَارِفِ is visible above the mim's fatha.
[الممتحنة:٤] is printed tight, with no word space between the colon and ٤.
The print shows the hamza with a fatha on the alif of the lam-alif. The Tanzil encoding ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ renders exactly this. B's ءَا would put the hamza on the line.
[البقرة:٢٠١] is printed tight, with no space after the colon.
At 2000 dpi, a single fatha and a small high mim (iqlab) are printed over the mim of قآئما. This is encoded قَآئِمًۢا as in Tanzil.
At 1500 dpi the final ba of فاكتب has only its dot below and no kasra. The damma on the ta and the sukun on the kaf are printed. Print error kept.
[التحريم:٨] is printed tight, with no space after the colon.
[الحشر:٢٢-٢٤] is printed tight, with no space after the colon.

At 1000 dpi the colon touches the digits and «](» is set closed up, so there is no word space. European digits are kept, and the range is in logical order 1-4 (1 is on the left in the print). ثلاثًا has no fatha on the tha.
At 1000 dpi the spacing is tight as in d022, and a fatha on the first tha of ثَلاثًا is clearly visible (unlike the Ikhlas line).
No waqf sign is printed after مِّنْهُ before the closing bracket. The quote ends there, so this is a genuine print variant.
No waqf sign is printed after ٱللَّهِ. The quote ends at the bracket (print variant).
No waqf sign is printed after مَعَادٍ. The quote ends at the bracket (print variant).
In the print, لَنَآ is followed directly by إِنَّكَ with no ۖ above it (checked on the crop and the zoom), so this is a genuine print variant.

print_errors.note: The initial mim carries shadda+damma in print (expected مُظَفَّرًا). Kept as printed; checked at 1000 dpi. The same pattern occurs on p.064 (مُّؤَزَّرًا).
قَوِيٌ is printed with dammatan only, no shadda on the yeh (expected قَوِيٌّ). Checked at 1400 dpi. Kept as printed.
The ra of الْمُرسَلِينَ has no sukun in print, while the parallel words الْمُذْنِبِينَ and الْمُتَّقِينَ are fully vowelled. Checked at 2000 dpi. Kept as printed.
The ain of نعتك carries a fatha in print (expected sukun: وَنَعْتِكَ). Checked at 1600 dpi. Kept as printed.
The final ba of فاكتب has no vowel (kasra) in print. Checked at 1600 dpi. Kept as printed.
66:8 has no waqf sign ۖ after لَنَآ in print, although Tanzil has one. Checked at 1300 dpi. Not added. scripts/quran.py flags it (quran_marks).

keyA.notes: Markers: p.064 ends with a full sentence (…[آل عمران: ١٦٠].) on a short last line, and the first line of p.065 is indented, so p.065 has no '+'. p.066 starts with an indented new prayer. p.067 continues the 2:201 quotation begun at the end of p.066 (its first line is not indented), so it is <<<ص:067+>>>. p.068 starts with an indented new paragraph (Ayat al-Kursi). Paragraph breaks follow indents or short last lines. The text of p.066 para 4 starts after the short line «…شَفَاعَتِهِ.» without an indent. Cross-page Quran quote: the 2:201 quotation runs from p.066 into p.067. Because validate.py requires balanced brackets on every line, it is closed with ﴾ at the end of p.066 («﴿رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى﴾») and reopened with ﴿ at the start of p.067. Neither bracket is printed at the page break. Bold: the parenthesised invocations on p.065 «وَأَيِّدْنِي بِكَ لَكَ», «وَاجْمَعْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ», «وَحُلْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ غَيْرِكَ» and «الله. الله. الله» are printed bold. The parentheses themselves have the same stroke width as regular parentheses (measured 24 px at 1500 dpi in both), so they stay outside the markers: (**…**). The rest of pp.065-068 is regular weight. The word Allah: on p.065 the body-font ligature (shadda and small alif drawn automatically) also carries a printed damma, so following CONVENTIONS §2 (case vowel printed, «write them all», e.g. اللَّهُ) it is written اللَّهُ (6 times). The bold «(الله. الله. الله)» has no case vowel, so it is plain الله. Explicitly vowelled اللَّهُمَّ (shadda+fatha drawn) on pp.066-067 is written with marks. Dagger alif over final alef maqsura in the body font (حَتَّىٰ، عَلَىٰ، الْهُدَىٰ) is written ىٰ as printed. Quran (Tanzil encoding): the round silent zero on أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ، ءَامَنُوا۟، صَلُّوا۟، وَسَلِّمُوا۟، وَأُو۟لُوا۟ (checked at up to 2000 dpi; it differs from the khāʾ-head sukun). A hamza on a seat drawn below the tooth with kasra (ئِ in أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ، ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ، وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ، قَآئِمًۢا) is encoded ئِ as in Tanzil. Hamza on a kashida seat is kept as Tanzil ـَٔ / ـُٔ (فَـَٔامَنَّا، سَيِّـَٔاتِنَا، يَـُٔودُهُۥ). The lam-alif with hamza+fatha in الآخرة (2:201) is encoded ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ (Tanzil form, which looks identical in this font). The iqlab mim on قَآئِمًۢا and أَحَدٌۢ (112:4) is printed and encoded with tanween + ۢ. Waqf signs are transcribed where printed. The signs Tanzil has at the end of a quoted span (58:22 مِّنْهُ, 16:53 ٱللَّهِ, 28:85 مَعَادٍ) are not printed and not added. scripts/quran.py reports only those 3 and the 66:8 لَنَآ case (see print_errors). Basmalas before al-Ikhlas and al-Falaq on p.068 are written in the standard form outside the brackets, on the same paragraph line as printed. References: spacing after the colon follows the print ([المجادلة: ٢٢], [الفجر:٢٧-٢٨], [البقرة:٢٠١], [الممتحنة:٤], [الحشر:٢٢-٢٤], [التحريم:٨] without a space; the others with one). A space is always written between ﴾ and [ and before ﴿ (on p.067 «عَذَابِكَ﴿يَوْمَ» is set nearly touching). European digits on p.068 are kept: the print shows the block «1–5» (1 on the left, 5 next to the colon), so the logical order is written [الفلق:1-5] and [الإخلاص:1-4]. Measured gaps (about 1.5 pt after the colon, about 2-3 pt elsewhere, comparable to digit side-bearings) show no word space after the colon or between ] and (ثلاثا). So the refs are written «[الإخلاص:1-4](ثلاثًا).» and «[الفلق:1-5](ثَلاثًا).». This differs from the illustrative «[الفلق: 1-5]» in CONVENTIONS §2, so an adjudicator should check that spot. The two «ثلاثا» differ in print: the Ikhlas one has fathatan only, the Falaq one also has a fatha on the first tha. p.065 مَدَارِجِ: the kasra under the final jim is printed. It sits just above the shadda/damma of صَلُّوا۟ on the next line. Kashidas (e.g. لَـكَ، قَـوِيٌ، البقـرة، كَـتَبَ) are dropped. Ornament flowers on the Quran brackets, running heads and page numbers are omitted.

print_errors.note: آل عمران ١٨: the print shows a plain fathatan on the mim with no small iqlab mīm (the Madinah mushaf / Tanzil has قَآئِمًۢا). Transcribed as printed.
التحريم ٨: no waqf sign (ۖ) printed after لَنَآ although the mushaf has one. Transcribed as printed.
المجادلة ٢٢: the print has no waqf sign after مِّنْهُ (the mushaf has ۖ). Transcribed as printed.

keyB.notes: p065 marker uses '+' : its first line (وَأَيِّدْنِي بِكَ لَكَ) starts flush at the margin and continues the dua paragraph of p064 (which ends with [آل عمران: ١٦٠].). p067 uses '+' because the Quran quotation ﴿رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ... is split by the page turn; since validate.py requires balanced ﴿﴾ on every line, the bracket is closed at the end of p066 (﴿رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى﴾) and reopened at the top of p067 (﴿ٱلدُّنْيَا ...﴾ [البقرة: ٢٠١]) — the print has one continuous quotation. p068 has no '+' (p067 ends with [التحريم: ٨]. and p068 starts a new block). Bold: on p065 the parenthesised phrases (وَأَيِّدْنِي بِكَ لَكَ)، (وَاجْمَعْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ)، (وَحُلْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ غَيْرِكَ) and (الله. الله. الله) are printed in a heavier face than the surrounding text, like the parenthesised phrases on p064, and are marked **…** including the parentheses; nothing else in the batch is bold. The word الله: the bold (الله. الله. الله) carries only the font's automatic marks → written الله; the six following occurrences carry a printed damma → written اللَّهُ per CONVENTIONS §2 example. On p066 the lam of the definite article is printed WITHOUT a sukun wherever the font uses the lam-mim / lam-kha / lam-ha ligature (المُرْسَلِينَ، المُتَّقِينَ، المُحَجَّلِينَ، المُذْنِبِينَ، الخَيْرِ، الهُدَىٰ، بِالمَعَارِفِ) while it is printed with a sukun elsewhere (الْغُرِّ، الْأَوَّلِ، الْأَغْيَارِ …); transcribed as printed (checked at 1000-1600 dpi). Dagger alif printed on ordinary (non-Quran) words (حَتَّىٰ، عَلَىٰ، إِلَىٰ، الهُدَىٰ) is kept as U+0670. وَأَوْجَبَ عَلَيْكَ الْبَيَانَ on p065 is set in the Uthmani font but outside ﴿﴾ → plain text; its alif has no wasla sign. Quran encoding follows the Tanzil table: silent alif/waw ۟ (U+06DF), small waw/yeh ۥ ۦ, waqf signs ۚ ۖ ۗ as printed, hamza-on-tatweel forms فَـَٔامَنَّا / سَيِّـَٔاتِنَا / يَـُٔودُهُۥ with the tatweel kept (it carries a mark). References keep the book's European digits on p068 ([الإخلاص: 1-4]، [الفلق: 1-5]) and the logical order of ranges (٢٧-٢٨، ١٩٣-١٩٤، ٢٦-٢٧، ٢٢-٢٤); a space is written after the colon in every reference although some are printed tight ([الفجر:٢٧-٢٨]، [الممتحنة:٤]، [الحشر:٢٢-٢٤]). Kashida stretching in [الـبقرة]، وَكَـفِّرْ، شَهِـدَ، ٱلْحَكِـيمُ، كُـلِّ etc. dropped. The basmala before الإخلاص and الفلق on p068 is printed in the small calligraphic form on the same line as the surah → written بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ outside the brackets, same paragraph.
